question: Besides keeping the skin clean, what is a key benefit of bathing a bedridden patient?

options.A: Preventing the patient from ever developing a fever
options.B: Completely eliminating the need for any pain medication
options.C: Stimulating blood circulation and assessing skin integrity
options.D: Lowering the patient's blood pressure permanently

explanation: Great job thinking clinically! Moving the skin and tissues gently during a bath boosts blood flow and gives you a wonderful chance to spot early signs of bedsores. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T2#GNS112_U5_T2_h1)

question: Why is the time spent bathing a patient so great for building the nurse-patient relationship?

options.A: It forces the patient to follow every single hospital rule without arguing
options.B: It gives the patient a chance to voice hidden fears and ask questions
options.C: It allows the nurse to complete all nursing documentation for the shift
options.D: It proves to the doctor that the nurse can complete physical tasks quickly

explanation: Spot on! That quiet, one-on-one time makes patients feel safe and cared for, often opening up about worries they wouldn't share in a busy hallway. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T2#GNS112_U5_T2_h1)

question: What is the main medical goal of giving a patient a sitz bath?

options.A: To lower a very high fever using freezing cold water
options.B: To increase joint flexibility in patients with severe arthritis
options.C: To reduce pain and swelling in the perineal and rectal area
options.D: To scrub off dead skin cells from the entire body surface

explanation: You've got this! A sitz bath focuses warm water right on the lower trunk to soothe discomfort from things like hemorrhoids or childbirth. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T2#GNS112_U5_T2_h2)

question: What is a crucial safety rule to remember when giving a therapeutic or medicated bath?

options.A: Leaving the patient completely unattended so they can relax
options.B: Making the water as hot as possible to open up the pores fully
options.C: Avoiding the use of any towels after the patient steps out
options.D: Limiting the bath duration to prevent skin maceration and exhaustion

explanation: Remember, soaking too long can waterlog fragile skin and totally wear out a patient who is already weak from illness. Keep an eye on the clock! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T2#GNS112_U5_T2_h2)

question: When giving a bed bath, what is the golden rule for the direction of washing?

options.A: From the feet upward toward the face
options.B: From the left side of the body to the right side
options.C: From the back of the body to the front
options.D: From cleanest areas to dirtiest areas

explanation: Always wash from clean to dirty! This simple habit stops germs from spreading from high-contamination zones, like the perineum, up to sensitive areas like the face. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T2#GNS112_U5_T2_h3)

question: Before giving an elderly patient a bed bath, what is the very first water safety check you should do?

options.A: Test the temperature with a bath thermometer or the inner wrist
options.B: Boil the water for twenty minutes to kill all bacteria
options.C: Let the water sit in the open air until it turns ice cold
options.D: Ask the patient to taste a drop of the water from the basin

explanation: Safety first! Always test the water with your inner wrist or a thermometer first. Elderly patients might not feel heat well, putting them at risk for nasty burns. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T2#GNS112_U5_T2_h3)

question: Which type of bath is best for a newborn baby before their umbilical cord stump falls off?
explanation: Spot on! Sponge baths keep the belly button area dry and clean, which helps the cord stump heal safely without getting infected. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T2#GNS112_U5_T2_h4)

question: Why must an infant never be left alone in a baby bath tub, even for a split second?

options.A: The water will instantly turn freezing cold without human body heat
options.B: Infants can drown in very shallow water due to lack of head control
options.C: The plastic tub will melt if nobody is touching it
options.D: Infants will climb out of the tub and run down the hospital hallway

explanation: Babies have heavy heads and wobbly necks. They can slip under even an inch of water and inhale fluid in seconds, so never turn your back on them! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T2#GNS112_U5_T2_h4)

question: How long should children wash their hands with soap to properly get rid of germs?
explanation: Twenty seconds is the magic number! Singing a short song helps kids scrub long enough to break down the germs on their skin. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T2#GNS112_U5_T2_h5)

question: What is the main goal of hygiene care for older school-age children compared to babies?

options.A: Forcing the child to bathe without any adult assistance whatsoever
options.B: Teaching the child how to operate heavy plumbing valves
options.C: Encouraging safe self-care and independence under supervision
options.D: Eliminating the need for soap entirely

explanation: You got it! School-age kids are ready to learn good hygiene habits themselves while we supervise to make sure they stay safe. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T2#GNS112_U5_T2_h5)

question: Why are daily full-body soap baths usually not recommended for frail elderly patients?

options.A: Elderly patients are completely immune to body odors
options.B: Water damages their internal organs through the skin pores
options.C: Their skin loses natural oils and becomes dry and irritated
options.D: Soap makes their bones become fragile and brittle

explanation: As skin ages, it makes fewer natural oils. Daily harsh soap and scrubbing can strip away what's left, leading to painful, dry, cracked skin. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T2#GNS112_U5_T2_h6)

question: When washing a patient's arms or legs during a bed bath, why does the nurse stroke from the hands or feet toward the torso?

options.A: To check if the patient has broken bones in the hand
options.B: To push all dirt and sweat directly into the armpits
options.C: To make the skin stretch out and look younger
options.D: To promote venous blood return toward the heart

explanation: Brilliant! Moving your washcloth upward helps push venous blood back up toward the heart against gravity, which is great for circulation. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T2#GNS112_U5_T2_h6)
